comparison: Perfect agreement on immunity protein findings (C49, C50). Both evaluations accept the data showing TsiP interacts with and neutralizes both TseP domains without challenge.

Perfect agreement on functional separation of structural and enzymatic roles (C51-C54). Both accept the complementation data showing TsePH339A restores T6SS function. Peer review notes desire for more discussion on biological significance of dual activity organization.

Perfect agreement on domain modularity (C55-C57). Both accept that amidase inactivation doesn't affect lysozyme activity. Peer review suggests more interpretation on evolutionary advantage of domain fusion.

Perfect agreement on homolog distribution and validation (C58-C60, C100). Both accept phylogenetic analysis and biochemical validation of representative homologs as establishing TseP as founding member of new effector family.

Strong agreement on amidase activity residing in N-terminal domain (C27, C42-C44). Both evaluations accept UPLC-MS data and catalytically inactive mutant controls as convincing evidence. Peer review emphasizes this as major novel finding.

Strong agreement on Zn2+-dependent amidase mechanism (C45-C48). Both accept convergent evidence from sequence analysis, mutagenesis, EDTA inhibition, and metal rescue experiments. Peer review highlights this as significant contribution.

Strong agreement on TsePN structural role in T6SS assembly (C35-C39). Both accept secretion assays, microscopy, and Western blot data. OpenEval also addresses VgrG2 interaction (C41) which peer review mentions briefly.

Strong agreement on crystal structure and distinctive features (C67-C71, C74, C76). Both accept 2.27Å structure and structural basis for substrate specificity. OpenEval also addresses E663D mutation requirement (C77) which peer review accepts.

Agreement on domain fusion evidence (C30, C61-C66) but different confidence levels. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting alternative explanations not excluded. Peer review accepts the fusion hypothesis without objection, though notes evolutionary questions about biological advantage remain unaddressed.

Strong agreement on TseP's novelty as dual-functional effector (C87, C90, C99). Both accept comprehensive characterization establishing unique combination of activities. Peer review emphasizes this as main finding with significant contribution to T6SS understanding.

Agreement on differential PG digestion patterns (C78-C80). Both accept that TseP/TsePC digest NaOH-treated but not native B. subtilis PG. Peer review focuses more on engineering implications while OpenEval emphasizes mechanistic interpretation.

Agreement on structure-guided engineering expanding substrate range (C81-C83). Both accept rational design based on electrostatic calculations. Peer review strongly endorses this work, noting it reveals general principles for lysozyme engineering.

Strong agreement on TsePC4+ gain-of-function against Gram-positive bacteria (C84-C86). Both accept secretion and co-culture data. Peer review highlights this as first modification of T6SS effector for expanded target range and notes therapeutic potential. Reviewer notes discussion of whether TsePC4+ retains Gram-negative activity should be in main text.

Agreement on priority claim for Gram-positive lysing effector (C116). Both accept this as first demonstration. Peer review emphasizes significance for antibacterial development while OpenEval focuses on experimental validation.
Agreement on VgrG2 interaction data (C40-C41). Both accept pull-down assay results. Peer review mentions this as part of thorough characterization but doesn't elaborate separately.

Agreement on E663D mutation abolishing activity (C77). Both accept this supports requirement for glutamate's longer side chain in wider active groove. Peer review accepts this as part of structural characterization.

OpenEval addresses EF-hand motif findings (C109-C110), noting negative mutagenesis results leave function uncertain. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - this detail was not specifically discussed by reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates background claims on antimicrobial resistance (C1-C6) as well-supported by literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation - reviewers did not separately assess background/context claims.

OpenEval evaluates T6SS and PG-targeting effector background (C7-C21) as appropriately supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation - reviewers accepted contextual framing without separate assessment.
OpenEval evaluates study system background claims (C22-C26) as supported by prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation - reviewers did not separately assess these foundational claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims about effector diversity and rarity of bifunctional effectors (C92-C98) as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation, though Reviewer 1 notes this is 'not the first dual domain effector' without challenging the characterization.

OpenEval evaluates claims about Zn2+ regulation and differential toxicity (C101-C104) as supported, noting inference about regulation is reasonable but not directly demonstrated. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these specific interpretive claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims about metal ion dependencies and potential misidentification (C105-C108) as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation - reviewers did not separately assess these comparative/interpretive claims.

OpenEval rates future application claims (C117-C118) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are speculative without supporting data. Peer review mentions therapeutic potential positively but doesn't separately evaluate these forward-looking claims as distinct from demonstrated results.
